name: Roxanne Shanté
hook: A 14-year-old from Queensbridge answered a record she didn't like and touched off more than fifty response records, hip-hop's first great beef.
blurb: Lolita Shanté Gooden, born in Queensbridge in 1969, was 14 when she recorded 'Roxanne's Revenge' (1984), produced by a then-unknown Marley Marl, answering UTFO's hit 'Roxanne, Roxanne' in character. It is one of hip-hop's first real diss and answer records. With no major label behind it, it sold hundreds of thousands of copies in the New York area alone, at a time when few women rapped solo at all, and made her a star before she was old enough to work full-time. It set off the Roxanne Wars, by some counts more than fifty answer records from other artists, some of the earliest evidence that a rap record could be a public conversation rather than a fixed, final statement. She became one of the first women to build a career as a solo rapper, and later a member of Marley Marl's Juice Crew.
